social_security.summary: Tennessee has no personal income tax; its only income tax (the Hall tax on interest and dividends) was repealed from 2021, so Social Security is not taxed by the state.

sources.quote: The Hall Income tax was repealed for tax periods that begin on January 1, 2021, or later.

public_pension.summary: Tennessee has no personal income tax, so government pensions are not taxed by the state.

sources.quote: The Hall income tax is imposed only on individuals and other entities receiving interest from bonds and notes and dividends from stock.
The Hall Income tax was repealed for tax periods that begin on January 1, 2021, or later.

private_pension.summary: Tennessee has no personal income tax, so private pensions, 401(k) and IRA distributions are not taxed by the state.

sources.quote: The Hall income tax is imposed only on individuals and other entities receiving interest from bonds and notes and dividends from stock.
The Hall Income tax was repealed for tax periods that begin on January 1, 2021, or later.

military_retirement.summary: Tennessee has no personal income tax, so military retired pay is not taxed by the state.

sources.quote: The Hall Income tax was repealed for tax periods that begin on January 1, 2021, or later.

notes: Tennessee has no statute index in this copy of lexflow, so only page sources are used. Tennessee never taxed wages, pensions or Social Security; its former Hall income tax reached only interest and dividends and was repealed for tax periods beginning on or after January 1, 2021. The tn.gov page was read from an Internet Archive capture (Aug 2026) because the live site's robots.txt refused automated readers.
